Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

description:
Mexico has been fighting against drug cartels for decades.
And its leaders have sometimes mobilised the military to dismantle their vast criminal operations.
This week, Mexican forces killed the leader of one of the country's most powerful drug gangs. 
His killing immediately set off a wave of violence across the nation, putting its security at serious risk.
Successive Mexican presidents have camapaigned on curbing the flourishing illicit drug trade and resulting violence.
But how have drug cartels managed to keep their hold on Mexico and some other countries in Latin America?

Sergio Aguayo -- Professor at the College of Mexico, specialising in organised crime

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The largest aircraft carrier of the United States Navy, the USS Gerald R Ford, has docked at a NATO base on the Greek island of Crete as it heads toward the Middle East.
The US has been increasing its military presence as tension remains high between Washington and Tehran. 
Donald Trump's repeatedly threatened military action on Iran if a deal isn't reached on its nuclear programme. 
The White House says Trump's first option is always diplomacy. 
Iranian and US officials are preparing to hold a third round of talks in Geneva later this week.

Meanwhile Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) has been conducting military drills in the south of the country.
The exercises are aimed at testing the readiness of Iranian forces in the event of an attack.
The Revolutionary Guard says it’s built “a strong fortress” in the area.

Anti-government protests have taken place in universities across Iran for a fifth day. 
Students have clashed with pro-government supporters in Tehran.

title: Largest US aircraft carrier nears Middle East as Iran steps up military drills

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Russian foreign policy analyst Andrey Kortunov believes “the territorial dimension is not the most important one” in the conflict in Ukraine.

“Of course, it is something the Russian leadership can claim as a victory – that Russia will have four more regions and a additional couple of million people,” he told Al Jazeera from Moscow.

Kortunov said that the Russian leadership maintains that “the West ignored Russia’s interests” and it was “marginalised in the European security system”.

According to the analyst, Moscow believed NATO was expanding to Russia’s borders and this movement had to be stopped.
